verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes JST connector coverage for panel touch, button, and reset inputs and requires an on-board BOOT button.
The client explicitly adds a panel switch to the required input hardware.
The client defines the connector-to-GPIO mappings, reset wiring, touch controllers, and development-only BOOT-button placement.
The freelancer identifies a material hardware-layout uncertainty between board-mounted buttons and connector-attached panel buttons.
The client resolves the hardware connection mode by requiring panel buttons through connectors and allowing only BOOT directly on the board.
The client resolves the blocking button-mounting ambiguity, allowing implementation of the panel-input interface to resume.
The source concerns a PWRON panel-power connector, which belongs to the separate panel power-control Requirement rather than this panel-input Requirement.
The source approves general connector placement on the integrated board and does not specify or relocate a PWRON power-button connector.

missing_event_candidates.description: The client requests a two-pin JST-GH connector that taps PWRON for an enclosure-mounted power button.
The exchange establishes acceptance and constraints for connector placement on the integrated board.
